_note: Translators whose death year has been checked against a source, for the rights gate. A translation's copyright term runs on the TRANSLATOR's death, not the author's — so a translated work cannot be shelved unless its translator appears here with verified: true. Keys are the normalised translator name; the ingest matches on the surname and given names it finds in the edition's own record or its repository slug. Nothing is added here on memory alone.

_schema.name: the translator as credited
_schema.death: year of death — drives the India test (life + 60)
_schema.verified: true only when a source below was actually read
_schema.source: where the death year came from

george-makepeace-towle.name: George Makepeace Towle
george-makepeace-towle.source: Wikipedia, George Makepeace Towle — died 9 August 1893, Brookline, Massachusetts; translated Verne's Around the World in Eighty Days, 1873

benjamin-jowett.name: Benjamin Jowett
benjamin-jowett.source: Wikipedia and Balliol College archives — died 1 October 1893; Dialogues of Plato translated 1871

james-legge.name: James Legge
james-legge.source: Wikipedia, James Legge — died 29 November 1897, Oxford; Sacred Books of the East, 1879–1891

george-long.name: George Long
george-long.source: already recorded on the shelved Meditations record; Long's Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius were published by Bell & Daldy in the 1860s–70s

constance-garnett.name: Constance Garnett
constance-garnett.source: Wikipedia (died 17 December 1946, The Cearne, Kent), Britannica and Orlando/Cambridge all give 1861-1946; her Chekhov volumes, The Tales of Tchehov, Chatto & Windus, ran 1916-1922

the-modern-library.name: The Modern Library
the-modern-library.source: a publisher credit, not a translator — the anonymous translator is unidentified, so this can never pass
